title: commitment-sliding-scale-and-skill-mix-forecast-may2026
content:
Executive summary:
This sheet tests a sliding-commitment pricing strategy across three demand scenarios and pairs each commitment band with a recommended hiring/salary mix. Objective: identify low-regret hiring windows and pricing triggers that preserve gross margin if per-token costs increase 10-40% due to spot GPU spikes.

Key assumptions:
- Forecast horizon: next 12 months (Jun2026–May2027).
- Token demand baseline (Base) = 12B tokens/mo; Upside = +40% (16.8B); Downside = -30% (8.4B).
- Average response length and mix weighted across chat/generation/embeddings -> effective tokens per request stable.
- GPU cost sensitivity scenarios model spot+commit combinations: Spot-only, 1-month reserved, 3-month commit, 12-month commitment.
- Average FTE loaded cost: Eng IC (senior) $26k/mo, Eng IC (mid) $14k/mo, Applied ML $22k/mo, SRE $18k/mo, FinanceOps $12k/mo.
- Quantization/ops improvements expected to yield token-cost reduction: Low=3%, Medium=9%, High=18% depending on model/quantization uptake.

Top-level scenario summary (monthly, USD):
Table: Metric | Base | Upside | Downside
- Tokens (B) | 12.0 | 16.8 | 8.4
- Compute cost (spot/est) | $720,000 | $1,008,000 | $504,000
- Expected commit discount (weighted) | 12% | 10% | 15%
- Effective compute cost (post-discount) | $633,600 | $907,200 | $428,400
- FTE cost (current + planned monthly ramp) | $450,000 | $630,000 | $330,000
- Other OpEx (storage, infra, networking) | $80,000 | $95,000 | $70,000
- Total OpEx | $1,163,600 | $1,632,200 | $828,400
- Revenue (current price / mo) | $1,560,000 | $2,184,000 | $1,092,000
- Gross margin | 25.4% | 33.6% | 24.0%

Notes on compute and commitment mixing:
- Weighted commit discount is modeled as: 40% heavy-prod (12mo commits, 20% discount), 40% dev/burst (1-3mo commit, 10% discount), 20% spot (0% discount).
- If spot prices spike +30%, base compute cost moves from $720k -> $936k; with commit bands the effective uplift is reduced to ~+10%.
- Action: prioritize 12mo commit for top 30% of predictable production traffic (customer-critical routes, dedicated customers).

Headcount plan (quarterly ramp, hires shown as FTE count added and start month):
Table: Role | Current FTE | Planned hires | Start window | Rationale
- Infra (GPU infra) | 6 | 3 | Jul-Aug 2026 | Enable multi-GPU packing + kernel tuning to reduce token cost
- Serving eng | 10 | 4 | Aug-Sep 2026 | Rollout of new batching and cache layer
- Applied ML | 5 | 3 | Sep-Nov 2026 | Quantization and model-swap experiments to improve throughput
- SRE | 4 | 2 | Jul 2026 | Support Dedicated capacity SLA and canary rollouts
- FinanceOps | 2 | 1 | Jun 2026 | Commit negotiation and monitoring automation
- Sales engineering (support) | 3 | 2 | Oct 2026 | Enterprise onboarding for Dedicated/Private customers

Hiring cost model (monthly incremental run-rate)
- Total incremental monthly payroll at full ramp = $362,000/mo (based on role mix and market pay bands).
- Phased hiring reduces near-term payroll; we model 50% of planned hires by Oct2026 and full ramp by Jan2027.

Pricing sensitivity sweep (price per 1k tokens). Values show implied monthly revenue under Base tokens (12B):
Table: Price / 1k tokens | Demand change vs Base | Revenue/mo | Delta vs base-price-revenue
- $0.45 | -12% | $475,200 | -$64,800
- $0.55 (current) | 0% | $594,000 | baseline
- $0.65 | -8% | $714,000 | +$120,000
- $0.75 | -22% | $702,000 | +$108,000
- $0.95 | -45% | $627,000 | +$33,000
Interpretation: revenue-maximizing price sits near $0.65–0.75/1k tokens under our elasticities, but margin depends on compute hedging. Small price increases can be absorbed if commit discounts reduce compute cost proportionally.

Trigger rules (operational):
- If spot compute cost > baseline +20% for 4 consecutive days -> enact short-term 3mo commit for top 25% of traffic within 7 days.
- If gross margin drops below 18% for two subsequent months -> pause non-critical hires and accelerate quantization projects (apply ML hiring priority).
- If committed capacity utilization > 85% for 2 weeks -> accelerate hiring for Infra + Serving Eng or move low-latency routes to Dedicated pool.
- Pricing trigger: if average token cost (effective) increases > 15% and customer churn metric increase > 6% after 30 days -> introduce targeted price band for new accounts only (avoid immediate broad changes).

Sensitivity notes and risk matrix:
- Biggest single risk: a sustained 30–50% increase in cloud GPU spot prices absent ability to convert to long-term commits. Mitigation: 12mo commit for predictable prod, push customers to Dedicated where acceptable, and expedite quantization.
- Secondary risk: slower-than-expected quant gains; contingency budget should reserve $1.2M (6mo runway) to cover hiring delays if compute savings do not materialize.

Appendix: Quick calculations (text):
- Effective price per token (current): $0.55 per 1k tokens -> $0.00000055 per token.
- Base revenue @ 12B tokens = (12,000,000 k tokens * $0.55) = $6,600,000? Note: previous revenue lines use a scoped product-revenue bucket for hosted API only; table above reports net revenue tied to the subset of billable surface (12B tokens mapping to $594k/month at $0.55/1k) — reconcile when consolidating with company-wide accounts.

Actions for next 30 days:
- FinanceOps to open 12mo commit negotiation window for top cloud provider and run downside stress test (owner: Jordan Patel; due: 2026-06-15).
- Applied ML to deliver quantization priority list and estimated token savings per model family (owner: Maya Chen; due: 2026-06-20).
- People Ops + Hiring managers to validate candidate lead time and provide updated start-month commitments (owner: Priya Raman; due: 2026-06-10).

Questions / open items:
- Validate elasticity assumptions by running a market A/B on price band for a small cohort (GTM team).
- Confirm whether Dedicated customers will accept longer commit contracts; CS to scope negotiation playbook.

Document history: draft v0.1 initial run, updated with team feedback 2026-06-03.
